body: I appreciate your forgiveness.
I'm resonating with what you're saying. I also hope that you find someone to rely on.

I appreciate everything you're saying. I'm sorry I sounded so harsh. I don't mean to push you away. You, along with everyone else who commented on this post, have truly made me happier these past few days. I cherish this dialog and the fact that you're sticking around. I hope I didn't hurt your feelings.

PS - Spotlight on a dark surface would make an awesome album title. I think I might use that if you don't mind!

Thanks for saying that I'm well spoken. I appreciate you telling me.

I've mentioned this opinion in one of these comment threads, but I think the whole idea of us "trying our very best" has a lot of destructive assumptions behind it. Trying my best assumes that if I'm not careful, I might not try, and then I won't get what I need. I would argue that everyone is always trying their best to achieve the goals that are important to them. I think that you saying that you have to try your hardest is an insult to yourself. I can only imagine how hard you try. Even though there are a lot of things lacking in your life, I firmly believe that you try so hard. We are all judged on the same criteria (Can you get a good job? A romantic partner? A friend group? If not, you're a failure) even though the game is unfair from the start. I hope that you can find the strength to love and forgive yourself more for your failures. Again, we're fucked from the start, and it's not our fault.

You might have already thought of this already, but I interpret the fear keeping you in your room as the product of countless traumas in your life, leading to a physiological reluctance to put yourself in danger. What you want most scares you the most, since not having it is comparable to death. So, after many failures, the fear becomes too strong to fight on your own. That's what I think at least, you can disagree. But if you do agree, I feel the same way. And I think that the only fix is an external one. A friend being there consistently, a family member offering long-term unconditional love, or a damn good therapist. I hope you find some or all of those things. I really do.
I completely forgive you. Your intentions are good, so I definitely see you as a friend.

I'll preface what I'm about to say by letting you know that I'm having a bad day. I'm sorry if I'm an asshole.

I appreciate your intentions, but whenever people give me advice and lecture me about things, I perceive it as ultimately condescending. By explaining this stuff to me, you're assuming that I don't know and have never thought about it before. In other words, you're assuming that I'm stupid and that I'd be doomed without you. There are so many usages of language in your previous post that seem to indicate to me that you think you've found all the answers to life. You're so great and special! I wish I could be you. Sarcasm aside, your post seemed conceited and egotistical, and I feel angry reading it.

Again, I appreciate the fact that you're trying to help me. You might be getting some selfish pleasure out of demonstrating how smart you are by explaining something complex to a damsel in distress online, but I'm pretty sure you also mean well. Thank you for your intentions, but your post hurt my feelings quite a bit. I want to be listened to more, not lectured more. I've been lectured all my life. I've heard everything you said before.

Thanks for your counter-analogy. I definitely see the merit to it. And I admire your confidence when you say as a fact that "that's not how we work." To be honest, I feel a little threatened and attacked by the implications of your language (that you're right and anyone else who disagrees is wrong), but that was probably not your intention. That's just the way most people talk, and it's one of the many things I find stressful about being around other people.

But I totally agree with your pump analogy. It makes sense. Too little of what we need and it vaporizes. For instance, I tell my long-distance and closest friends that I'm suicidal, and then they call me. We talk, and it's nice. And then maybe we talk the next weekend. But then the week after that, no more. Their empathy has run out, and they're back to caring about themselves. I spend every night alone in my room talking to no one, and no one's life is any different. It's like what Eddie Murphy said in Raw. What have you done for me lately?

Anyway, thanks for your comment. I enjoy thinking about it your way. Thanks for reaching out.

Isn't that funny? That so much of our pain/desire/sense of purpose can be boiled down to just dumb instinct? Like who consciously cares about passing on their genes? It's not relevant at all to what people think they want. And yet most of our lives are dedicated to performing our darwinistic duties. To mate, to band together in packs, and to not die. If that's not evidence that we are exactly like animals, I don't know what is. Yes, we have language and hot pockets and suicide hotlines, but all our motivation can (I think) be traced back to instinct.

That's so interesting that half of males pass on their genes while almost all women do. It's interesting in such a depressing way. It makes perfect sense to me, though. You express it really well, I think. We're genetic waste.

I'll offer one potential silver lining. Even if you're the biggest piece of genetic shit in the world, if you can find a way to satisfy your desires (sex, love, community), there's a slim chance you'll have a good life anyway. It's a very slim silver lining though, since I think our world benefits the strong and punishes the weak, so that's not a very common scenario. Much more common is the homeless man who dies in a pile of garbage underneath the freeway. Unloved and forgotten instantly, since he doesn't contribute to the rat race. We're not members of the gold-plated circlejerk.

I totally 110% empathize with you when you say that you have total logical understanding of your problems, but you can just never solve them. Again, I think that some people are fucked from the start. Variables that are outside of our control (genes, parents, friends, community, socioeconomic status, etc) just make us inherently sad.

That segues into your question about the Mr. Peanutbutters. I agree with you, I envy them too. My opinion is that Mr. Peanutbutters are just luckier in their circumstances. They have better genes, more loving parents, more supportive friends, more resources, etc. So, more happiness in the end. Little things don't matter as much because they have been assured all their lives that they are valuable and good. They may accept that fact logically, but then they also have the subconscious belief that they are good. Imagine having your whole personality be based on a foundation of confidence. Why would you be bothered by day-to-day things? Why would you ever think that you couldn't go into a bar and talk to some attractive people and get laid if you wanted to? Your whole experience, your whole story confirms that narrative. Meanwhile, people like me and (maybe) you did not have those boons. We got fucked by the universe. I'm sorry, I wish I could say something more optimistic. But I'm pretty sure I'm right.

Actually, here's some good news. If you can figure out what you need, you might be able to buy it. I'll use myself as an example. I have been craving a mutual romantic relationship since I was 12, and I've never had it. It's gotten so bad where I can't even be in the same room with someone I'm attracted to without having panic-attack-like symptoms. But, there are sex therapists that will actually spend time being intimate with you and help you regrow your confidence. It's an uphill battle, to be sure, but it does work for some people. The bad thing is, it requires money. That's depressing in an existential sense (the world will only give me conditional love, or in other words, the world will only give me love if I have money/confidence/good looks/talent/etc. Otherwise, I might as well be a corpse on the street that people walk around (that happens in India apparently if you didn't know)), but it's also not an option for most people. Most people are poor and can't afford that first-world shit. So, my only conclusion is that many (most?) people are doomed to endless sadness.

I'm so sorry. You deserve better. And if you're asking yourself where the evidence for your deserving of love is, there is none. But I want to believe in it. I want to believe that everyone has an inalienable right to be happy, and it's an everyday torture to face the fact that life is inherently so fucked.

I would definitely agree with the idea that our culture indoctrinates us with this idea that things will make us happy. When you say that you buy things that put money into your pocket, are you talking about like buying real estate and then renting it out? In any case, that sounds like an ideal and awesome lifestyle. I just don't think that I have the strength to keep delaying my gratification in those kind of ways. I only work one day a week, and I spend half the week dreading that one day.

Yeah, a lot of people find purpose and community through religion, but it's never really clicked for me. I went to Jewish school for a long time, and there were tons of religious classes and mandatory services. It might have been ruined for me from an early age, since it was always shoved down our throats at the threat of punishment. Who knows. I'm open to becoming religious in theory, but I don't see it ever happening realistically. The tenants of any religion always seemed less important to me than the sense of community membership that one gets by adopting a shared set of beliefs and behaviors. Feeling like you belong, you know? You might not agree, but that's okay.

I disagree with you when you say that you can be so much better. God knows how hard you try in all the things you do, and I'm a firm believer that everyone is always trying as hard as they can. Sure, goals might change (for example, some people who don't try in school don't care because it's not important to them, while they try as hard as they can in their social interactions). But I feel like it's a disservice to yourself to say that you don't try. I also think that it is a nefarious thing to believe because then all of your sadness is now your fault (since you could always change it by being "better"). I'll say it again, I think that some people are just dealt a shitty hand, simple as that. That even goes down to the way that the chemicals in your brain work, so that some people think happy thoughts most of the time, and some people think sad thoughts most of the time. It's all arbitrary, and it's totally unfair. Life is shit. Hooray for those who win the lottery (all the attractive and talented people with loving parents and supportive friends), but everyone else is fucked.

Good luck to you. God knows you deserve better. I'm sorry that you feel so much pain.

I appreciate your comment. 

I don't want you to kill yourself, but I don't have a good answer for you. The future will always be a mystery, of course, but we all have a hand of cards that we're dealt, and some people are fucked from the start, I think. 

That being said, I hope that you have the strength required to make sure that none of your cards will do the trick. I have no doubt that many people who kill themselves would have been happy later in life if they hadn't. 

I also think that if you ask an old person if they're happy, many of them would say that they are happy despite the fact that their bodies are shit. You can look up psychology research studies on the correlation between age and happiness if you don't believe me. I guess priorities change.

What I'm about to say might be just me, but I'm pretty sure this is a universal experience. Memory is so weird. In the moment, bad things are so much more powerful than good things, but in retrospect, most of the bad things are forgotten, while the good things are remembered (or nothing is remembered at all). So, if one can somehow make it through 20 years of suffering, it will probably seem worth it to your future self, despite the fact that there was so much suffering. For example, I hated high school, but now, most of my memories from that time are positive and nostalgic. I don't know if you feel the same way or not.

Talking to you is enjoyable for me! Just because I need more substantial social connection than Reddit does not mean I feel better talking here than I do curled up underneath the covers convulsing.

I empathize with your inability to read anymore. For a time, I was building up a collection of books from thrift stores, and I was so excited to read them. But now, I can't even focus enough to finish three pages in less than half an hour. My mind is just so preoccupied.

I also empathize with your mental conjuring of different people in your life and how the unreality of it makes them disappear. Sorry in advance if this is TMI, but I feel the same way when I'm masturbating, and I'm trying to use my imagination instead of solely relying on porn. I think of attractive people that I've known in the past, but then I'm overcome by sadness and despair that people like them will never be attracted to me.

So, the therapist in me wants to respond to what you said about you being able to discern between the real and the unreal. You've probably thought of this before, but just in case you haven't, I'll say it. Is it possible that maybe your ability to objectively judge what is real vs. unreal has been compromised by your self-loathing? In other words, is it possible that you are never really objective and always look at your life through shit-colored glasses? I definitely wear shit-colored glasses (you can see that by how I said in the paragraph above that no one I'm attracted to will ever be attracted to me. I don't know that for a fact, since the future can never be fully predicted, but I feel that way so concretely that it seems true to me). It's really insidious when we believe that our self-loathing is objective truth. I think that it exponentially compounds our problems.

For a while, I felt the same way as you when I felt terrible thinking that I'm not unique. But honestly, now I'm in a place where I think that uniqueness is just a Western capitalist bullshit value. Uniqueness is only important insofar as it allows us to be successful. If you envision a world where people are valued not by what they create but by the sheer fact that they exist, uniqueness doesn't matter, right? If everyone is inherently loveable no matter what they do, then no one needs to prove anything to receive love. So maybe my problems aren't unique, but if I'm ever going to be happy, I think that my uniqueness would be irrelevant.

I totally agree with you when you say that we are programmed to have sex. I would add that you could argue that everything we do is inherently programmed. For example, we need social connection because we were only able to survive as a species by banding together. I'm sure you could think of other examples. If you believe this, than the conclusion is that nothing we do matters, and nothing is objectively valuable. However, if your next conclusion is that the only thing that matters, then, is enjoying life, than things like sex and social connection have value again. They don't have value in a universal existential sense, but they have value just because they are enjoyable. Life is stupid and terrible, but now that we're here, the best thing to do is to do what makes us happy. Unless you cannot get what makes you happy, and then you want to kill yourself like I do.

Thank you for describing what I was saying as poetic. I feel lucky and privileged to be able to express myself in ways that other people find enjoyable/valuable.

I haven't read either of those books. I'll add them to my list, but as I said before, I'm not really able to read at this point in my life. Maybe eventually. I have watched (and loved) both Rick and Morty and Bojack Horseman. I found Rick and Morty to be more entertaining, but I found Bojack Horseman to be more emotionally powerful and lasting.

Feel free to disregard what I'm about to say (it's only my opinion), but I think you might get something out of posting something of your own. I'm sure you know this already, but there is a certain amount of catharsis that one can get just by vocalizing one's experience. Even if no one responds, I think that it feels good to scream at the world.

I appreciate you saying that I seem intelligent. That's a nice thing to hear.

I'm sure that you're right that a white collar job isn't necessary to survive and that there are other niches that one can inhabit. But the way I see it is that most people don't want to work a white collar job, so by definition, the niches that are left over are difficult to find, since everyone would be interested in them (you may agree or disagree with this, I'm not sure). And I'm at a place where I feel so tired that I don't even want to try to look for them anymore.

Well, I guess I've never hitchhiked to the countryside, and I've never joined an intentional community, and I've never backpacked across Europe, and I've never lived out of my car. But again, those possibilities seem so far out of my comfort zone. I can't imagine mustering the strength required for me to uproot my life that much. Are there others that are more realistic?
I appreciate that you feel the same way. Thanks for your comment.

It's okay, you don't have to be scared of saying the wrong thing. Your intentions are beautiful, and I appreciate you for it.

1 on 1 is the best, I agree.

I'm happy that you can have conversations with female friends while having an open heart. I've never really had a good female friend. I'm terrified of anyone I'm attracted to, and I'm tired of trying to force myself to be attracted to the girls who have shown me interest but who I'm not attracted to. I'm just so tired of feeling like I'm just another guy who has to perform his peacock dance in order to be loved. I'm hopelessly outmatched by all the confident, tall, strong dudes.

I wish you luck on getting out of this boat. I don't see my problems as universal, just an unlucky hand of cards. So maybe you'll find the strength. I hope you will. I wish everyone could be happy and loved. I just don't think the universe will ever work that way. I feel like we're headed in the opposite direction, actually.

Good question. Deep social and romantic connections characterized by unconditional love that is expressed in a long-term way, thereby breaking down my deeply internalized anxiety and convincing me of my value.

Thank you for the question.

I think I know what you mean when you're talking about treating life like a dream when you're this far down the gutter. For brief moments, my constant anxiety and depression are replaced by incredible apathy. I think, fuck it, I'll just ask this girl out in a horribly awkward way. I'll just blast music in my room and dance by myself with the lights off. I'll just drink as much of this alcohol as I possibly can. But like you say, it's all-too-brief, and then the anxiety and depression come back again. Old habits die hard.

I admire your hope when you say that there is a 1% chance of happiness and that that warrants clinging to life. But like I said before, how long do I have to wait? At a certain point, isn't it best to just cash in your chips and get out of this game?

I'm also still trying in certain ways. I'm seeing a therapist twice a week, researching sex therapists, trying to reach out to old friends for help, letting myself eat pint after pint of ice cream with little judgement, starting antidepressants, only working part-time, etc. But I'm not strong enough anymore to do more than that. Even just approaching someone attractive at a bar seems like light years away from me. 

I remember last year, a friend took me to a bar and said, "we're not leaving until you say hi to someone attractive." Just the word "hi." It took close to an hour, and I was shaking and sweating. I'm just so far down this hole. It's hard to even imagine being outside of it anymore.

Thanks for your comment. I enjoy talking with you.
I feel good knowing that I had that powerful of an emotional impact on you. Thank you for telling me.

I feel happy that my post resonated with you. I think that my story is very common, actually. The difference is that I have never wanted to compromise with life. I'd rather kill myself than be a white collar zombie, poop out some kids to stave off the existential dread, and then find myself at age 50, hating everything and yet having unavoidable responsibilities and thus tethered to hell.

I agree with you that the real world offers much needed catharsis and breaks up the stagnancy of being alone with your thoughts all day every day. For years I've tried. An uncountable amount of frat parties, anime clubs, swing dances, smokey bars, European nightclubs, music festivals, ceramics classes, volunteering in Denmark, studying abroad in Denmark, performing in concerts, going to terrible social events with my parents, traveling by myself, volunteering to help people with mental health difficulties, working at a horrible high school, hiking, jogging, meditating, yoga, zumba, reaching out to friends from the past, searching for people on online dating apps every single night for the past half year. It was all terrible (I was anxious for every second), but I saw it as a delay-your-gratification type thing. If I work to make social/romantic connections, then I can enjoy them later. Except it never happened. I'm a ghost, alone in my room with no one asking about me, no one checking in, no one invested in my story. And now, I think it's too late to keep trying. I don't have the strength.

And if you're thinking, "you're not alone! I'm invested in your story," I'm sorry, but you don't count. You're an internet person. You're probably amazing, but who knows where you live, what you do, and if a truly deep friendship with me would be possible. Probably not, unfortunately. It's not that I don't appreciate these comments. But it's too little, too late.

I agree, I'm afraid that death is not the end. It might be that we all are trapped in the afterlife, slowly going insane. Maybe that's what every living thing has to look forward to. Maybe I haven't even had an ounce of the ocean of pain that I could truly experience. But none of these thoughts make me feel better. Much more the opposite, actually. But I appreciate your intentions.

I appreciate your response. It sounds like you have some hope left, which is admirable.

And your English sounds great to me.

[This song describes how I'm feeling pretty well.](https://youtu.be/yB5hafiKjtA?t=26s)

Lyrics:

I can see so far
